key_insight: CATTS (Conditionally Allocated Test-Time Scaling) dynamically assigns extra inference compute to the most consequential steps of multi-step agent tasks, reducing error compounding and yielding higher returns than uniformly increasing sampling at every step.
problem_solved: Uniform test-time scaling (e.g., more sampling everywhere) gives diminishing returns on agentic, multi-step tasks because small per-step errors compound over long horizons; the paper addresses how to allocate scarce inference compute where it most reduces downstream failure.
method: Empirical analysis showing per-step errors compound over agent rollouts and that naive uniform scaling has diminishing marginal benefit.
A dynamic compute-allocation scheme (CATTS) that detects high-impact or high-uncertainty steps and concentrates extra sampling/compute on them instead of spreading budget uniformly.
Budget-aware deployment so overall inference cost is respected while improving end-to-end task success.
impact: CATTS makes multi-step agents (e.g., web agents, planners) more reliable and compute-efficient by focusing resources where they most reduce failures, enabling better performance without a proportional increase in inference cost.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of an agent executing multiple steps with variable-width bars showing per-step compute allocation (uniform vs CATTS).
Line chart comparing task success vs total inference compute for uniform scaling and CATTS (showing higher slope for CATTS).
Schematic illustrating error compounding over steps and how targeted extra compute clips the error growth.
Icon set: compute budget (chip), uncertainty gauge (meter), checklist for end-to-end task success (trophy).
paper_authors: Nicholas Lee, Lutfi Eren Erdogan, Chris Joseph John, Surya Krishnapillai, Michael W. Mahoney
